newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Suranyi says Hungary rate cuts not a loosening.
newsitem.headline: Suranyi says Hungary rate cuts not a loosening.

text.p: National Bank of Hungary (NBH) chairman Gyorgy Suranyi said this week's cuts in repo rates and state bond yields did not indicate a loosening of interest rate policy.

"In terms of tightness, the policy remains absolutely unchanged," Suranyi told Reuters Financial Television in an interview broadcast on Thursday. "If you have an interest rate of about 20.75 percent, a quarter percent reduction cannot be taken as a signal of loosening."

On Monday the NBH surprised markets by cutting its one-month and one-week reverse repo rates by 25 basis points to 20.50 and 20.00 percent in the morning, then reducing its one-week and overnight repo rates by 0.25 percentage point both to 26.00 percent.
The rate cuts were completed by the reduction of the one-year NBH bond yield to 20.03 percent from 20.27.

Analysts and traders said NBH president Gyorgy Suranyi's earlier remarks on "a cautious interest rate policy" had weakened repo rate cut expectations and the NBH moves caught part of the market players unguarded.
"In the last few years we have gradually reduced the repo rates which is in line with the actual and expected rate of inflation," Suranyi said.
Inflation ran at 17.7 percent in May and the NBH said in a recent statement June inflation was likely to be between 17.4 and 17.8 percent.

Analysts agreed that the rate cuts projected a stagnation or a drop in inflation in June and they said pending revisions of May household savings figures by the NBH and April current account data expected for Wednesday were likely be positive.
